evidence.quote: Inflation remains above the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) 2 percent target, and further progress on disinflation has been slow.
Given the upside risks to inflation and given that I still view our policy stance as somewhat restrictive, I supported the decision to keep rates at that level.
Several other economic indicators that I track suggest some signs of declining economic activity in the future.
I believe it is critical to keep long-term inflation expectations very well anchored at 2 percent.
I view our current stance of monetary policy as well positioned for any changes in the macroeconomic environment.
Ultimately, I see the U.S. as likely to experience lower growth and higher inflation.

parsed.rationale: The speaker supports holding rates, cites upside inflation risks from tariffs and rising inflation expectations, but also flags slowing growth and a policy stance already somewhat restrictive. On net the guidance is wait-and-see with a slight hawkish tilt from the inflation concerns.
